product.name: PT-141 (Bremelanotide)
product.description:
### PT-141 (Bremelanotide)

**Central Melanocortin & Neurobehavioral Signaling Research**

PT-141, also known as bremelanotide, is a synthetic cyclic peptide belonging to the melanocortin receptor agonist class. It is studied for its interactions with melanocortin receptor systems, particularly MC3R- and MC4R-associated signaling pathways involved in central neuroendocrine and neurobehavioral regulation.

Laboratory research involving PT-141 may examine receptor-binding characteristics, G-protein-coupled receptor signaling, intracellular cyclic AMP pathways, and interactions between melanocortin signaling and central neural regulatory networks.

PT-141 is structurally related to Melanotan II but has a distinct pharmacological and clinical research history. Bremelanotide is also the active ingredient in an FDA-approved prescription medication, making its regulatory classification an important consideration when distinguishing genuine laboratory reference materials from finished pharmaceutical preparations.

**Research classification:** Melanocortin receptor agonist
**Primary research axis:** Central melanocortin signaling
**Secondary research axis:** Neuroendocrine and neurobehavioral biology

This entry is provided for scientific education and non-clinical research reference. It is not an administration protocol or a representation that a particular product is authorized for human use.

product.technicalOverview:
PT-141 is a synthetic cyclic peptide analog of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH). It acts as an agonist at melanocortin receptors, with research indicating preferential activity at the MC4 receptor subtype. The compound is studied for its role in modulating central nervous system signaling pathways involving melanocortin receptors.

In laboratory settings, PT-141 is used to investigate melanocortin receptor pharmacology, including receptor binding, activation, and downstream signaling cascades. Research models often explore its effects on neuronal circuits and behavioral endpoints in non-clinical studies. The peptide's stability and solubility properties make it suitable for various in vitro and in vivo experimental protocols.

This product is intended for research use only. It is not for diagnostic, therapeutic, or veterinary applications. All handling and experimentation should be conducted in accordance with institutional and regulatory guidelines for research chemicals.

related.name: AOD-9604
related.description:
AOD-9604 is a synthetic peptide fragment derived from the C-terminal region of human growth hormone studied in laboratory research for its interaction with metabolic signaling pathways and lipolytic regulatory models. Research investigations commonly examine receptor-independent signaling mechanisms and downstream intracellular pathway modulation in non-clinical environments.

This material is supplied for analytical testing and non-clinical investigational research applications. Format is provided solely to support controlled laboratory handling.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.technicalOverview:
AOD-9604 is a synthetic peptide corresponding to the C-terminal fragment of human growth hormone (residues 177–191) with an additional tyrosine residue at the N-terminus. It also circulates under the name Tyr-hGH fragment 176-191, and both stylings appear in supplier listings — they describe the same molecule.

The peptide was designed to reproduce the lipolytic region of growth hormone without the diabetogenic effects of the full protein. That framing is best read as design intent rather than a demonstrated result: the primary literature characterising the compound is analytical, and its functional claims are reported rather than established.

In vitro incubation in serum and urine has identified six potential metabolites. Of these, the sequence CRSVEGSCG proved significantly more stable than the parent compound itself — a useful inversion for method development, where the parent is not necessarily the best analyte to target.

Note that the unmodified hGH fragment 176-191 is a different peptide with its own CAS number, lacking the N-terminal tyrosine. The two are not interchangeable and should not be treated as the same material.
related.researchApplications:
Metabolite identification in serum and urine incubations
Trace-level analytical method development targeting the parent and the stable CRSVEGSCG metabolite together
Solid-phase extraction and LC-MS/MS assay validation
Comparative work against the unmodified 176-191 fragment to isolate the contribution of the N-terminal tyrosine
related.storageHandling: Store lyophilized vials at controlled room temperature away from light; keep tightly closed. For long-term storage, refrigerate at 2–8°C. Reconstituted material should be refrigerated and used promptly.

related.technicalOverview:
BPC-157 is a synthetic pentadecapeptide — fifteen amino acids — whose sequence corresponds to a partial fragment of Body Protection Compound (BPC), a protein isolated from human gastric juice. Unlike many research peptides, it has no counterpart circulating as a complete molecule in the body; the fragment itself is the research subject.

The peptide is notable for its stability. It resists degradation in gastric juice for over 24 hours, which is unusual for a peptide of this size and is one reason oral and intragastric routes appear so often in the animal literature alongside injection.

Nearly the entire body of evidence is preclinical — rodent and in vitro work from a small number of research groups, with wound, tendon, ligament, muscle and gastrointestinal injury models reporting accelerated recovery. Proposed mechanisms in these models include promotion of angiogenesis through VEGFR2 pathway activation, modulation of the nitric-oxide system, and upregulation of growth hormone receptor expression in fibroblasts.

The honest framing: no adequately powered human clinical trials have been published, so human efficacy and safety remain uncharacterised. The claims attached to this molecule should be read as hypotheses generated by animal work, not established results.

related.technicalOverview:
CJC-1295 without DAC is more precisely named Modified GRF (1-29), or tetrasubstituted GRF (1-29). It is a 29-residue analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone, built on the GRF(1-29) fragment - the shortest fully functional portion of GHRH, which is itself marketed as sermorelin - with four amino acid substitutions at positions 2, 8, 15 and 27.

The substitution that matters most mechanistically is L-alanine to D-alanine at position 2. Native GHRH is cleaved rapidly at its N-terminus by dipeptidyl peptidase-4 to an inactive fragment, giving GRF(1-29) a plasma half-life on the order of minutes. The D-Ala2 substitution makes that bond resistant to DPP-4, and modified GRF(1-29) is reported to have a substantially longer half-life as a result. It acts at the growth hormone-releasing hormone receptor (GHRHR) on anterior pituitary somatotrophs.

A naming caution that has practical consequences: 'CJC-1295' in the primary literature refers to the drug-affinity-complex (DAC) version, in which the peptide carries a maleimidoproprionyl linker that binds covalently to serum albumin, extending its half-life to days. That is a different molecule with a different formula, mass and CAS registry number. The human pharmacokinetic study most often cited for 'CJC-1295' (Teichman et al., 2006) studied the DAC version, not this one. Data from that work do not transfer to the no-DAC material.

The CAS number field has been left empty deliberately. Publicly available sources give conflicting registry numbers for the no-DAC compound (446036-97-1 and 863288-34-0 both appear), and neither could be confirmed against an authoritative chemical registry. Reporting a CAS number that may be wrong is worse than reporting none.

The honest framing on evidence quality: modified GRF(1-29) itself has essentially no published human clinical trial record. The GHRH-analogue class is well characterised in principle, and sermorelin and tesamorelin have regulatory approvals, but this specific tetrasubstituted analogue has not been through the trial process. Recent reviews of peptides used outside approved indications place it explicitly in the unapproved category with an uncharacterised safety profile.

GHRH receptor (GHRHR) binding and activation assays
Pituitary somatotroph cell culture and GH secretion studies

related.storageHandling:
Supplied as a lyophilised (freeze-dried) powder in a sealed vial. Store the unopened vial at -20 C for long-term storage; short periods at 2-8 C are acceptable for material in active use. Protect from light and keep the vial sealed until use - lyophilised peptide is hygroscopic, and allowing the vial to reach room temperature before opening prevents condensation on the powder.

Reconstitute in the laboratory with bacteriostatic or sterile water, or an appropriate buffer, directed down the vial wall rather than onto the powder; swirl gently and do not shake or vortex, as shear and foaming denature peptides. Once in solution, store at 2-8 C and use within a short working window; for longer holds, aliquot into single-use volumes and freeze at -20 C or below. Avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles - each cycle measurably degrades peptide integrity. For Research Use Only - not for human or animal consumption.

related.name: Cagrilintide
related.description:
Cagrilintide is a synthetic peptide analog studied in laboratory research for its interaction with amylin receptor signaling pathways and associated metabolic regulatory mechanisms. Research investigations commonly examine receptor binding dynamics, intracellular signaling responses, and downstream pathway modulation related to amylin-associated receptor activity in non-clinical environments.

This material is supplied in lyophilized research format for analytical testing, stability evaluation, and non-clinical investigational research applications. Lyophilized format is provided solely to support controlled laboratory handling and does not indicate suitability for clinical or veterinary administration.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.sequence: 37-residue amylin analogue built on a pramlintide-like backbone with substitutions at positions 14, 17 and 37 (N14E, V17R, P37Y), a C-terminal amide, and an intramolecular disulfide bridge characteristic of the amylin family. The N-terminus carries a C20 eicosanedioic fatty diacid attached through a gamma-glutamic acid linker, which is what confers albumin binding and once-weekly kinetics. A residue-by-residue sequence is not stated here because it could not be confirmed against an authoritative primary source.
related.technicalOverview:
Cagrilintide is a lipidated, long-acting synthetic analogue of human amylin (islet amyloid polypeptide). Native amylin is co-secreted with insulin by pancreatic beta cells and acts on receptors formed by the calcitonin receptor in complex with receptor activity-modifying proteins. Native amylin is unsuitable as a research or therapeutic molecule because it aggregates readily; the analogue chemistry here addresses both aggregation and clearance.

Pharmacologically, cagrilintide is described as a non-selective agonist across the calcitonin family of G protein-coupled receptors - it engages both amylin receptors and the calcitonin receptor, rather than being amylin-receptor selective. The C20 fatty diacid attached through a gamma-glutamate linker drives reversible albumin binding, which is the structural basis for its extended half-life.

Unlike most compounds in this catalogue, cagrilintide does have a substantial human clinical record. It has been studied in randomised controlled trials, most prominently in combination with semaglutide (the combination is referred to as CagriSema), with phase 3 results published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2025 for both overweight/obesity and type 2 diabetes populations. Network meta-analyses of obesity pharmacotherapy now include it.

The honest framing: the clinical data that exist are for the pharmaceutical product administered under trial conditions, not for research-grade material of unverified provenance. Most published efficacy data are for the cagrilintide-semaglutide combination rather than cagrilintide as a single agent, so monotherapy effects are less well characterised. As supplied here the material is a reference compound for laboratory work; nothing in the clinical literature transfers to it as an article of commerce.

related.name: Cerebrolysin
related.description: Cerebrolysin is a nootropic peptide preparation derived from purified pig brain proteins, used primarily in Eastern Europe and Asia to treat stroke, dementia, and traumatic brain injury. It acts as a neuroprotective agent to shield neurons from damage, stimulate repair mechanisms, and enhance cognitive function. It is administered via injection or infusion.
related.sequence: Not applicable - Cerebrolysin is a heterogeneous hydrolysate, not a single defined peptide. It has no unique amino acid sequence. It consists of low-molecular-weight peptides (<10 kDa) together with free amino acids.
related.technicalOverview:
Cerebrolysin is not a single molecule and cannot be described by one formula, mass or sequence. It is a peptide-rich preparation produced by controlled enzymatic hydrolysis of purified porcine brain proteins. Its composition is defined by specification rather than by structure: roughly 15 percent of the nitrogen content is peptide and roughly 85 percent free amino acids, with the peptide fraction restricted to species below about 10 kDa. Because it is a biologically sourced hydrolysate, batch-to-batch compositional variability is an inherent property of the material, and analytical characterisation (for example by nanoLC-MS peptide mapping) is an active research topic in its own right.

The proposed mechanism in the literature is that this mixture of low-molecular-weight neuropeptides partially mimics the actions of endogenous neurotrophic factors such as BDNF, NGF, GDNF and CNTF. It is important to be clear that this is a hypothesis about a mixture, not a characterised receptor interaction of a defined ligand.

The honest framing on evidence quality, which for this preparation is unusually well documented: Cerebrolysin has been used clinically for decades in parts of Eastern Europe and Asia, and a large number of trials exist. However, independent Cochrane systematic reviews have repeatedly examined that evidence and reached negative or inconclusive verdicts. The Cochrane review of Cerebrolysin for acute ischaemic stroke, updated across multiple editions, found no evidence of benefit on death or dependency and raised concerns about the risk of bias and the influence of trial sponsorship in the underlying literature. The Cochrane review for vascular dementia similarly found the evidence insufficient to support routine use. Meta-analyses in traumatic brain injury are more mixed but rest on heterogeneous, largely small trials.

In short: this is a compound with a long clinical history and a weak independent evidence base. Descriptions of it as an established neuroprotective agent are not supported by the highest-quality systematic reviews available. It is supplied here strictly as a research reference material.
related.researchApplications:
Analytical characterisation of peptide hydrolysates (nanoLC-MS, peptide mapping, batch comparison)
In vitro neuronal culture and neuroprotection assay systems
Comparative studies against other brain-derived peptide preparations
Animal models of ischaemic injury, seizure and neuronal death

Formulation and solution-stability studies of complex peptide mixtures
related.storageHandling:
Supplied as a sterile aqueous solution in sealed 5 ml glass ampoules. Store ampoules at controlled room temperature (15-25 C / 59-77 F), protected from light, in the original carton. Do not freeze - freezing and thawing an aqueous peptide hydrolysate promotes aggregation and precipitation. Do not use an ampoule whose contents are discoloured, cloudy or contain visible particulate.

No reconstitution is required; the material is already in solution. Ampoules are single-use by design - once opened, the contents are no longer sterile and no preservative is present, so any unused volume should be discarded rather than retained. If dilution is needed for an assay, prepare it immediately before use. Handle glass ampoules with appropriate protection when snapping the neck.

For Research Use Only - not for human or animal consumption.

related.technicalOverview:
GHK is a naturally occurring tripeptide, glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine, first isolated from human plasma. Its defining chemical property is a high affinity for copper(II); the physiologically and experimentally relevant species is the 1:1 copper complex, GHK-Cu, which is what this product supplies. The free tripeptide and the copper complex carry separate CAS registry numbers and separate formulae, which is a common source of confusion in supplier documentation - both are given above.

Plasma GHK concentrations decline substantially with age, which is the observation that originally motivated research interest. Reported activities in cell culture and animal models include modulation of extracellular matrix turnover - both collagen synthesis and metalloproteinase activity - copper delivery to cells, antioxidant effects, and broad changes in gene expression. Gene-expression profiling work has reported that GHK influences a large number of human genes, which is frequently cited but should be read as a hypothesis-generating transcriptomic observation rather than a demonstrated mechanism.

The honest framing on evidence quality: the mechanistic literature is largely in vitro and rodent work, and a notable proportion of the widely cited reviews originate from a small number of authors closely associated with the compound's commercial development - a pattern worth weighing when reading the secondary literature. Human evidence exists mainly in the cosmetic and dermatological domain and consists of small studies of topically applied formulations; recent reviews of topical GHK are explicit that skin penetration, formulation stability and dose standardisation remain unresolved problems. There are no large, well-controlled clinical trials establishing systemic efficacy for any indication. Copper-containing compounds also carry their own handling and toxicology considerations that are distinct from those of ordinary peptides.

Reconstitute in the laboratory with bacteriostatic or sterile water, or an appropriate buffer, directed down the vial wall rather than onto the powder; swirl gently and do not shake or vortex, as shear and foaming denature peptides. Once in solution, store at 2-8 C and use within a short working window; for longer holds, aliquot into single-use volumes and freeze at -20 C or below. Avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles - each cycle measurably degrades peptide integrity. Copper-peptide complexes are additionally light- and oxidation-sensitive: use amber vials or wrap in foil, avoid contact with strong chelators, and note that solution colour change (the complex is characteristically blue) can indicate dissociation or degradation. related.technicalOverview:
Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide growth hormone secretagogue developed at Novo Nordisk. It acts as an agonist at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor GHS-R1a - the ghrelin receptor - on pituitary somatotrophs, and is mechanistically distinct from the GHRH analogues (sermorelin, tesamorelin, modified GRF 1-29) which act at a different receptor.

The characteristic that defines it in the literature is selectivity. The original characterisation paper described ipamorelin as the first selective growth hormone secretagogue: it produced robust, dose-dependent increases in plasma growth hormone in animals and humans while, unlike earlier secretagogues such as GHRP-6 and GHRP-2, showing minimal effect on ACTH, cortisol and prolactin. That clean hormonal profile is the reason it remains a useful pharmacological tool for isolating GHS-R1a-mediated GH release from confounding pituitary effects.

The honest framing on evidence quality: ipamorelin's receptor pharmacology is genuinely well characterised - this is not a compound with an unclear mechanism. Its clinical history, however, is a record of failure. It reached phase 2 trials under Helsinn Therapeutics for postoperative ileus and was discontinued for lack of efficacy. It has no regulatory approval anywhere. There is no clinical evidence supporting its use for body composition, recovery, or anti-ageing purposes, and recent reviews of unapproved peptide therapies place it explicitly in the category of compounds with insufficient human safety and efficacy data. It is also prohibited in competitive sport. There is additionally no published evidence bearing on oral bioavailability, which is a distinct question for a solid dosage form.

related.storageHandling:
Supplied as a lyophilised (freeze-dried) powder in a sealed vial. Store the unopened vial at -20 C for long-term storage; short periods at 2-8 C are acceptable for material in active use. Protect from light and keep the vial sealed until use - lyophilised peptide is hygroscopic, and allowing the vial to reach room temperature before opening prevents condensation on the powder.

Reconstitute in the laboratory with bacteriostatic or sterile water, or an appropriate buffer, directed down the vial wall rather than onto the powder; swirl gently and do not shake or vortex, as shear and foaming denature peptides. Once in solution, store at 2-8 C and use within a short working window; for longer holds, aliquot into single-use volumes and freeze at -20 C or below. Avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles - each cycle measurably degrades peptide integrity. For Research Use Only - not for human or animal consumption.

related.name: JB-1-S
related.description:
Semaglutide is a synthetic peptide analog studied in laboratory research for its interaction with glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor signaling pathways. Research investigations commonly examine receptor binding behavior, signal transduction mechanisms, and downstream metabolic signaling models in non-clinical settings.

This material is supplied for analytical testing, reference standard comparison, and non-clinical investigational research applications. Format is provided solely to support controlled handling and material consistency in laboratory environments.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.sequence: A 31-residue analogue of human GLP-1(7-37) carrying three defining modifications: alpha-aminoisobutyric acid (Aib) substituted at position 8, which blocks DPP-4 cleavage; lysine to arginine at position 34; and a C18 fatty diacid attached at the position-26 lysine through a gamma-glutamate and two short PEG-like spacer units. A residue-by-residue listing is not reproduced here.
related.technicalOverview:
JS-GLP-01 is a vendor reference code; the compound is semaglutide, as stated in the product description. Semaglutide is a long-acting agonist of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor, a class B G protein-coupled receptor, engineered from the native incretin hormone GLP-1.

Three structural changes carry the pharmacology. Native GLP-1 has a circulating half-life of a couple of minutes because dipeptidyl peptidase-4 cleaves it near the N-terminus; substituting alpha-aminoisobutyric acid at position 8 removes that cleavage site. The C18 fatty diacid attached through a gamma-glutamate and spacer at Lys26 confers strong reversible albumin binding, which both shields the peptide from renal clearance and further slows degradation - this is the change responsible for once-weekly kinetics. The Lys34-to-Arg substitution ensures the acyl chain attaches at a single, defined position.

Semaglutide has one of the most substantial clinical evidence bases of any compound in this catalogue. Cardiovascular outcomes have been assessed in a large randomised trial in obesity without diabetes (SELECT), efficacy for weight loss in multiple randomised trials and meta-analyses across adult and adolescent populations, and it has been compared head-to-head with tirzepatide. Effects in specific populations such as knee osteoarthritis have also been examined in dedicated randomised trials. Safety has been reviewed systematically.

The honest framing, and it is important on an RUO product page: that clinical evidence describes the pharmaceutical product, manufactured and controlled to pharmacopoeial standards and administered under trial supervision. It says nothing about research-grade material of unverified identity, purity, aggregation state or endotoxin content. Peptide impurity profiles differ substantially between manufacturers, and analytical confirmation of identity and purity is a prerequisite for any meaningful laboratory work. This material is supplied as a reference compound for in vitro and analytical use only.
